title: Offline Trajectory Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning

problem.claim: Offline reinforcement learning aims to learn policies without online exploration, and model-based approaches use learned dynamics models to generate simulation data for policy learning.

gap.claim: Existing offline RL data augmentation methods provide only trivial improvement with short-horizon simulation and lack evaluation and correction mechanisms for generated data, resulting in low-quality augmentation.

narrative_sequence.summary: Offline reinforcement learning learns policies without online exploration.
Model-based offline RL learns a dynamics model and uses it as a virtual environment to generate simulation data for policy learning.
Existing data augmentation methods suffer from limited gains from short-horizon simulation and low-quality generated data due to missing evaluation and correction.

source_observation.claim: Generated training data can be low quality when augmentation methods lack mechanisms to evaluate and correct it.

interpretation.claim: Synthetic-data pipelines may require quality assessment and correction in addition to data generation.

application.claim: When using model-generated data for training, consider adding explicit evaluation and correction stages.

exception.claim: The supplied source units do not establish whether evaluation and correction improve outcomes in other settings.

unknowns: The proposed method and its specific contribution are not described.
